briefs.headline: How labourer’s tip-off & policeman’s curiosity busted drug racket in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The discovery of the alleged spurious-drug racket earlier this week began with a group of labourers working in an agricultural field and a curious constable who was willing to listen.
The labourers at CK Tandya village in Dodderi near Tavarekere in Ramanagara had been noticing something odd. A stockhouse bordering the agricultural land was regularly being used to dump what appeared to be medicine waste consisting of vials, tubes and strange packets filled with foul-smelling powders.
One of the labourers eventually decided to speak about it. He approached Shivaraj, a police constable attached to Tavarekere police station, and shared what he had noticed. Instead of brushing aside what could easily have been dismissed as a routine cribbing about waste dumping, Shivaraj took it seriously. He visited the spot in plain clothes, collected samples.
The act of curiosity eventually led Ramanagara police to uncover an alleged fake-drug racket involving the repackaging of spurious medicines as expensive products from 
Pfizer
 and other pharmaceutical companies.
“This was how we received the tip-off,” Ramanagara superintendent of police R Srinivas Gowda told 
TOI
. “Shivaraj’s basic policing skills of listening to a labourer and then acting seriously on it yielded the result.”
Shivaraj’s findings were subsequently discussed at a crime meeting. Deputy superintendent of police, Magadi division, P Ravi, and his team were tasked with finding out what was happening inside the stockhouse.
Their investigation revealed something far more serious than illegal dumping. There was a huge stock of medicines inside the warehouse. Police checked with medical officers to determine whether the premises was a licensed stockhouse or whether any legitimate medicine-related activity was being carried out there. The answer was clear: it was neither a licensed stockhouse nor authorised for any medicine-related work.
The police then raided the premises Tuesday.
Investigators allege that the racket involved procuring cheap, spurious medicines from Himachal Pradesh and Telangana and passing them off as products manufactured by pharmaceutical giant Pfizer.
According to police, medicines were being repacked and relabelled as Pfizer products before being sold for as much as Rs 7,000 per unit.
The investigation has so far led to the arrest of four people, while the alleged kingpin is in Dubai.
Police identified the alleged mastermind as R Prashant, 36, a medical representative and resident of Papareddy Palya, who is presently based in Dubai.
“Prashant leased the stockhouse from one Siddaiah around 11 months ago. He had worked as a medical representative in Bengaluru and different places in Telangana,” an investigating officer said.
Police suspect Prashant operated the racket with the help of pharmacist Venkatesh, proprietor of Bangalore Special Life in Chamrajpet. Cops said the duo sourced the fake medicines from Himachal Pradesh and Telangana.

briefs.headline: Two in Bengaluru assault lodge owner over ‘CSK’ name, get bail months later
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In a bizarre case where cricket rivalry spilled into real-world violence, Karnataka high court recently granted regular bail to two men who allegedly assaulted a lodge owner in Tumakuru after mistaking his business acronym for a tribute to Chennai Super Kings (CSK).
Justice S Vishwajith Shetty allowed the bail petition filed by Swamy, 38, and Suprith, 23, after nearly two months in judicial custody.
According to police records, the incident took place on June 1 within Tilak Park police limits in Tumakuru, shortly after an Indian Premier League match between Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Gujarat Titans.
The accused allegedly confronted lodge proprietor Ameen Ahamad CS, questioning why he had named his business ‘CSK Comforts’. The men allegedly mistook the three-letter signage for a reference to Chennai Super Kings, a fierce rival of RCB. Despite Ahamad clarifying that CSK was merely an abbreviation for his business and had no connection to the cricket team, the duo allegedly abused and assaulted him before damaging lodge property.
Ahamad subsequently filed a complaint, following which police registered an FIR under several provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Arms Act. 
Both men were remanded in custody the same day.
The accused later approached a local court for bail, but their plea was rejected. They then moved the high court under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, citing the progress of investigation.
The HC noted that Ahamad had suffered simple injuries, a major portion of the investigation was complete, and neither accused had prior criminal antecedents. It concluded that further pre-trial detention was unnecessary and ordered their release.
The court directed them to execute a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh each with a matching surety, cooperate with the trial and appear regularly. They were also barred from tampering with prosecution witnesses, committing similar offences or leaving the trial court’s jurisdiction without prior permission.

briefs.headline: Govt to take stock of H1N1 as Karnataka cases cross 4,000
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The state govt will hold a meeting with health officials this week to take stock of the 
H1N1
 situation, with 
Karnataka
’s tally crossing 4,000 cases this year, including more than 2,000 reported from Bengaluru alone.
Health minister U T Khader said surveillance and preparedness will be among the key issues to be discussed at the meeting, amid concern over the spread of the seasonal flu in Bengaluru.
Karnataka recorded 4,583 H1N1 cases during the whole of 2025. This year’s tally has already reached 4,125, with the seasonal peak expected to taper off only in Sept. Udupi has reported 293 cases, followed by Mysuru with 184.
The concern intensified this week after a city school was shut following H1N1 cases among its students. Health department data shows the Greater Bengaluru Authority area has reported 2,033 cases so far, while Bengaluru Urban district has recorded another 982. Together, the two areas account for more than half of Karnataka’s cases this year.
Doctors suspect the actual number of infections could be higher than reported, given that many people with mild symptoms may not undergo testing.
Dr Veena, deputy director of the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), said there was no need for panic, as surveillance mechanisms were already in place. 
“There is no need for panic with respect to H1N1. Surveillance is already in place and there is only a slight increase in cases compared to the previous year,” she said, stressing the need for greater awareness about hygiene and infection-control measures.
She also ruled out concerns over a mutant strain, saying laboratories had not detected anything unusual in the influenza A virus.
Explaining the mode of transmission, she said respiratory droplets could settle on surfaces and infect people who touch them and then fail to wash their hands before touching their face.
The health ministry, in an advisory posted on X, said H1N1 can cause fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue, and advised people with persistent symptoms to seek medical attention. Officials have also been asked to keep hospital logistics and other resources ready for admissions, including severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases, as several cities are reporting an increase in influenza cases.

briefs.headline: SIR reports 16.38 lakh deceased voters, four times Karnataka’s average annual deaths
briefs.deck: The scale of the electoral-roll figure raises a broader question on how long these names had remained on the rolls, and how many elections were conducted with the names of dead voters still appearing on the electoral rolls
briefs.bodyText:
Of the over 1.08 crore voters identified till August 17, under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead, and Other (ASDDO) categories in Karnataka, over 16.38 lakh have been marked as “dead” – the figure is nearly four times the average number of deaths recorded in the State in a year, according to an analysis of demographic estimates done for the period between 2002 and 2024.
While the comparison does not mean that 16.38 lakh people died in a single year, the scale of the figure is significant.
What SRS indicates
Between 2002 and 2024, Karnataka’s estimated total population deaths work out to around 98 lakh, or an average of about 4.45 lakh deaths a year, based on population estimates and the State’s annual crude death rates reported through the Sample Registration System (SRS). The highest annual estimate during this period was around 5.2 lakh in 2021, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The scale of the electoral-roll figure raises a broader question on how long these names had remained on the rolls, and how many elections were conducted with the names of deceased voters still appearing on the electoral rolls.
It is pertinent to note that the ECI printed over 5.44 crore enumeration forms based on Karnataka’s 2025 electoral rolls, after summary revision, taking that number as the electorate to be covered under the SIR.
Going by the State’s average annual death estimate of around 4.45 lakh – a figure that also includes deaths among those below 18 years and not just voters – the number of electors who would have died between the 2025 roll and the current revision would still be expected to be lower. Yet, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has identified more than 16 lakh voters as dead, nearly four times Karnataka’s estimated average annual deaths.
The figure also continued to change after the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) declared 100% digitisation of the enumeration forms. The ‘Dead’ category stood at 16.30 lakh on August 5, a day after the ASDDO list was made public, but rose to 16.38 lakh by August 17, when the enumeration phase ended.
The increase is significant because the Chief Electoral Officer has repeatedly maintained that deceased voters are being verified through death certificates or, where such documents are unavailable, a spot mahazar. If the enumeration data had been fully digitised, the rise in the number of voters classified as deceased also raises questions about when these cases were identified and how they were being added to the category.
Asked about the overall number and its increase, the Chief Electoral Officer said: “What we realised is that a large number of dead voters were on the rolls. But I cannot comment or have an opinion on the figures, as each case is accounted for with a death certificate or a spot mahazar.”
Wrongly marked dead
Even during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bihar, several cases emerged in which living voters were wrongly marked as “dead”. Activist Yogendra Yadav brought two such cases before the Supreme Court, highlighting how voters, who were alive, had been declared deceased.
Following this, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi met some voters who had been declared dead and had tea with them, pointing out that he had a unique experience of having “tea” with some of Bihar’s “dead” voters.

briefs.headline: Nearly 70% of Bengaluru’s white-topping projects miss deadlines, commuters at receiving end
briefs.bodyText:
Nearly 70% of the white-topping projects taken up in the city have missed their deadlines, while several others are likely to meet the same fate, according to Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) data.
Its adverse impact is on the city traffic, with multiple diversions in place and several key stretches being choked. Meanwhile, B-SMILE officials, who are in charge of the projects, maintained that several reasons, including approvals and multi-agency coordination, have contributed to the delays.
Krishna Byre Gowda, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister, presented the list of ongoing and delayed works in response to a question asked by MLA for Yelahanka S.R. Vishwanath.
The data shows that of the 78 white-topping works ongoing across the city, 54 are delayed. Some of the major delayed works include Hennur 80 Feet Road, Mosque Road, Sanjaynagar Main Road, and Hosakerehalli Main Road, among others.
Coordination issues
Sources in the B-SMILE maintained that getting approvals from multiple departments is still a challenge, which significantly contributes to the delays. The source pointed out that Kengal Hanumanthaiya Road has to be white-topped, but permission to close the road was denied by the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) more than twice before being approved recently.
However, according to sources in the Bengaluru Traffic Police, K.H. Road is a major link connecting different parts of the city, so closing it even partially would disrupt traffic. That is why the permissions were held back.
“They wanted to work on the J.C. Road, which was already delayed, and permission was again sought before the monsoon. We have asked them to complete the drain works first, after which, in phases, we can extend permission,” the source said.
However, the civic body points out that it is not just one agency but multiple agencies that work simultaneously, making it nearly impossible to complete works on time. In his response, Mr. Gowda said that when white-topping is taken up, water and sewer lines are reviewed and fixed, ensuring that there would be no instances of digging up the road again for the next 20 years.
While these works are to be coordinated, Mr. Gowda has noted in the past that coordination has historically been poor. He recently announced a new application that creates a single platform for different agencies to coordinate civic works.
Commuters’ struggle
The TomTom Traffic Index, a global assessment of congestion by a Dutch group, placed Bengaluru in second place, just behind Mexico City, on the list of the most congested cities in the world in 2025. The results also meant Bengaluru was the most congested city in India.
The BTP had then listed delayed civic works as one of the reasons that affect traffic in the city and triggering an increase in commute times. These delays directly impacted several key stretches in the city.
For instance, due to the delayed Panathur white-topping works, peak-hour traffic at the Marathahalli Junction had shot up drastically and triggered an extension of peak hours in the eastern part of the city until the road was opened. Similarly, Lower Agaram Road white-topping works triggered massive traffic disruption by choking a key link between the southeastern and central parts of the city.

stories.headline: Luxury sales plunge in China as tax push hits rich shoppers
stories.bodyText:
Global luxury brands are facing a deepening sales slump in China, as the country's campaign to tax offshore wealth sends ripples from stock markets to casino floors and dampens spending by the country's richest consumers. Sales at the 25 biggest luxury labels in China dropped more than 10% in July, according to three research firms surveyed by Bloomberg that track industry data. That's worse than the slowdown witnessed in June, and marks a sharp reversal from the brisk business seen earlier this year.
LVMH's Louis Vuitton and Dior, as well as Kering SA's Gucci, Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga all recorded double-digit sales drops, while Hermes swung from gains to declines, the people said. Growth for Chanel and Prada also decelerated significantly.
For global luxury giants, the declines add uncertainty to the outlook in one of their most important markets. China was once the engine of decades of luxury growth, but competition for the wealthiest shoppers has intensified and middle-class consumers have cut back on their spending amid the economic downturn.
The slump coincides with China's sweeping efforts to stem capital outflows and reclaim tax revenues, including tighter controls on cross-border stock trading and demands for citizens to pay billions of dollars in levies on offshore assets and investment gains. The steps have dampened the spending appetite of wealthy Chinese, threatening to unravel a luxury recovery that began less than a year ago.

stories.headline: Feedstock sourcing: The next critical lever for scaling CBG ecosystem
stories.deck: Press mud, agricultural waste as paddy and wheat straw, and animal manure are among the most widely used feedstock for producing CBG.
stories.bodyText:
While the Union Government’s latest push for Compressed Biogas (CBG) provides a more stable framework for offtake, industry observers and senior government officials say the next major imperative is to establish an efficient supply chain for procuring, storing and managing feedstock. This will be critical to ensuring both the viability of CBG plants and the quality of their output.
Press mud, agricultural residues such as paddy and wheat straw, and animal manure are among the most commonly used feedstocks for CBG production. However, each has its own logistical challenges, particularly because of seasonal availability, transportation requirements and storage constraints.
With the aim of accelerating the growth of CBG in India, the Union Cabinet on August 9 approved a revamped GOBARdhan (Galvanising Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) scheme with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore. The scheme, which will remain in place until 2036, seeks to increase CBG production nearly tenfold.
Speaking to The Hindu, Gaurav Kedia, Chairman of the Indian Biogas Association (IBA), emphasised that the type of feedstock and the proximity of a CBG plant to its source are crucial for ensuring a consistent supply. He also cautioned against long-distance transportation that could undermine the environmental benefits of CBG by increasing fossil-fuel consumption.
A senior government official similarly stressed that the quality of feedstock is critical, as it directly influences the quality of CBG produced and the long-term sustainability of a plant.
Press mud and cattle dung, according to Mr. Kedia, need to be sourced close to the plant because of their high moisture content and perishable nature. Paddy straw, by comparison, can be transported over longer distances, but it must first be baled and stored appropriately.
“Supply chain feasibility becomes important. We see [within] 25-km radius as a viable option,” Mr. Kedia said.
Cattle dung presents a further challenge because it is typically dispersed across a wide geographical area. Collecting and transporting sufficiently large quantities may therefore prove economically unviable. Press mud and paddy straw also pose seasonal supply challenges.
Press mud is the solid residue left after sugarcane processing. Since sugar mills generally operate for only four to five months a year, the material must be stored temporarily and transported to CBG plants in a timely manner.
Paddy straw, meanwhile, is available mainly during the harvesting periods of Kharif and Rabi crops. Collection must be completed within a short window—typically around 15 days—before farmers prepare their fields for the next crop. This makes rapid collection and field clearance essential.
Storage creates another set of challenges. Large quantities of agricultural residue must be stored in a manner that prevents fire hazards, particularly during the summer months. During the monsoon, the feedstock must also be protected from moisture, which can affect its quality and suitability for processing.
Another important component of the supply chain is farmer outreach. Mr. Kedia said an aggregator-based model could help bridge the gap between farmers and CBG plants.
“The prescribed model is to have an aggregator to supply the feedstock. Farmers may not want to enter into a legally binding contract like industries for social reasons, and this is where an aggregator pitches in to facilitate the outreach and supply [CBG plants] the feedstock,” he stated.
The senior government official said aggregators could also provide farmers with bio-slurry generated during the CBG production process, which can be used as an organic fertiliser.
Depending on the technology used, gas yield from cow dung is approximately 6%, while paddy straw and other agricultural residues can yield around 10% or more, they said, adding the resulting bio-slurry can subsequently be returned to farmers for use as an organic fertiliser, creating an additional link between CBG production and agricultural activity.
Industry observers and officials also recommend that CBG plants be designed to process multiple feedstocks rather than depend on a single source.
A diversified feedstock mix could make plants more resilient to seasonal fluctuations while improving their bargaining power in procurement, according to Mr Kedia.
The senior government official suggested that a plant having a complementarity of press mud and sugarcane could be an ideal set-up.

stories.headline: Amrit Bharat 3.0: AC coaches with Vande Bharat-style features for common man soon. Why it matters
stories.deck: Introduced in 2023, over 60-plus Amrit Bharat trains run across the Indian Railways network. The fares are around Rs 500 per 1,000 kilometres for sleeper class travel - the aim clearly being affordability.
stories.bodyText:
After upgrading train travel for the common man with Amrit Bharat Express, 
Indian Railways
 is now set to introduce air-conditioned coaches in the Amrit Bharat 3.0 Express, expected to be rolled out this financial year.
Up until now, the Amrit Bharat Express has been a non-AC long-distance passenger train with general class and sleeper class coaches. What differentiates the Amrit Bharat Express from other Express trains for the common man are its faster travel promise and Vande Bharat-style passenger amenities.
Introduced in 2023, over 60-plus Amrit Bharat trains run across the Indian Railways network. The fares are around Rs 500 per 1,000 kilometres for sleeper class travel - the aim being affordability.
Demand is clearly in place: As per Indian Railways data, the average occupancy in the sleeper class of Amrit Bharat trains is above 100%.
Amrit Bharat Express Features
Amrit Bharat Express trains boast of a locomotive at each end, with the train making use of the push-pull technology for higher speeds, faster acceleration and deceleration, cutting down the overall travel time for commuters with maximum speed of up to 130 kilometres per hour.
Amrit Bharat Express caters to journeys undertaken by the common man, workers, migrants, and also aims to cater to festive season rush while providing modern and somewhat premium passenger services.
Amrit Bharat Express Comfort
ICF Chennai has been given the order to manufacture 50 Amrit Bharat 2.0 trains, of which 32 have been rolled out and 18 more are expected this year. RCF, Kapurthala is also making 50 rakes.
Some of the major features of Amrit Bharat trains are:
- Foldable snack table
- Comfortable, improved seats & berths,
-  Streamlined-LED light fitting
- Fans with sleek SS grills
- Air spring suspension bogies
- Crashworthy features, electro pneumatic assisted brake system for quick brake application
- Public Address & Passenger Information System (PAPIS)
- Mobile holders, charging sockets USB A & C type ports
- Fully sealed gangway for quick coupling & decoupling, vacuum evacuation system similar to Vande Bharat
- Semi-automatic couplers instead of semi-permanent for easy attachment and detachment - this enables jerk-free rides
- Improved interior panelling with Aluminium Composite Panels
- Radium Illuminated flooring strip
- Foldable bottle holder
- 2 Indian & 2 Western style toilets in each coach with electro pneumatic pressurised flushing system
- Automatic-soap dispenser
- Toilet Indication light
- Best in class toilets for maintenance friendly & better aesthetics, Automatic hygiene odour control system in FRP Modular toilet
- External emergency lights to provide basic lighting during emergency situations
Toilets in Amrit Bharat Express
Amrit Bharat Express 3.0 Loading
Indian Railways is now manufacturing AC coaches to be fitted into the Amrit Bharat Express formation. Sources told TOI that the air-conditioned Amrit Bharat coaches will have several Vande Bharat sleeper and Rajdhani Express features to offer passengers a premium experience.
Also Read | 
Why India making its own bullet trains is a big deal - explained
They said that all three types of long-distance travel AC coaches are planned: AC 1st, AC-2 tier, AC-3 tier. For Amrit Bharat 3.0 with AC coaches, a total of 14 rakes have been ordered.
With AC coaches, Amrit Bharat Express trains will be similar to other Express trains that run for long-distance travel, albeit with modern passenger amenities, and Vande Bharat and Rajdhani-style passenger amenities.
But even as Amrit Bharat Express looks to upgrade train travel experience for general class passengers and keeps travel affordable, railway experts point to the need for more air-conditioned travel, and more train sets.
Amrit Bharat Express: Safety in focus
The Road Ahead For Indian Railways
Amrit Bharat Express will soon get AC coaches and experts note that the demand for air-conditioned travel is rapidly increasing.
In fact, Sudhanshu Mani, retired ICF GM and the man behind the Vande Bharat Express says Indian Railways should aspire to have only AC trains in the coming years so that common man’s train journeys can truly get an important upgrade.
According to Sudhanshu Mani, the train does not address the issue of how to seat the maximum number for passengers who are travelling long distances cramped and standing.
“An aspirational India should progressively look at replacing most trains with air-conditioned ones,” he believes.
G Raghuram, Advisor, The Infravision Foundation acknowledges that having two locomotives at each end helps on high density routes to avoid locomotive reversal.
Amrit Bharat Express: Smarter Design
“Having two locomotives at each end helps in acceleration/deceleration and speed on high density routes, and to avoid locomotive reversal. Passenger amenities have been upgraded and the faster express train travel are advantages,” he tells TOI.
“In a way Amrit Bharat is a new brand of trains, similar to the Janata, Jayanti Janata and Jan Shatabdi expresses that were introduced earlier, and then left to lose significance. I hope this brand survives,” he says.
But, he points out that in terms of second class primacy in the train, it should be recognised that the overall demand for AC train travel is increasing at a faster rate. Introduction of more AC coaches, even for the common man is the way to go, he says.
Shri Prakash, retired Railway Board Member draws on the success of the Vande Bharat trains, pitching for more trainsets in the coming years.
Also Read | 
Why India's first hydrogen train is special - explained
“Amrit Bharat trains offer faster acceleration and as a result transit time may reduce to some extent. But there is reduction in passenger carrying capacity from 24 to 22 coaches because of extra engine. Each train carries about 18 per cent less passengers,” he tells TOI.
“Going ahead, Indian Railways should go for a time-bound plan for replacement of all conventional passenger trains with trainsets which have distributed power like Vande Bharat or EMU trainsets. These are not only energy efficient but also they have operational convenience as well as improved riding quality,” he says.
Which is not to say that Amrit Bharat trains do not have their advantages. “You can Amrit Bharat a common man’s version of Vande Bharat which incorporates some frills like foldable snack tables, bottle holders, radium floor strips for visibility, and USB Type-A and Type-C charging ports and serves as a train for faster travel by those who cannot or will not afford Vande Bharat travel,” Sudhanshu Mani tells TOI.
“A good part is the use of semi-auto couplers freeing the train of jerks which persist on LHB coaches and which Indian Railways has not been able to eliminate,” he adds.
Indian Railways moves the nation, and it moves people across economic strata. Even as premiumisation happens, affordable rail travel is the underlying fundamental that the national transporter aims to hold on to.
With Amrit Bharat trains, better passenger amenities and faster travel is the goal - but as experts point out India should aspire to offer its people AC train travel as a basic amenity, and not a luxury. Though, this will obviously come with its implications for railway finances.

stories.headline: Partial FDI opening in e-commerce “almost worse” than no opening: Competere chief
stories.deck: The government in July 2025 eased its rules to mandate that FDI would be allowed in e-commerce companies that hold their own inventory as long as that inventory is only exported.
stories.bodyText:
India’s partial opening up of foreign direct investment (FDI) rules in the e-commerce sector could be “almost worse” for competition than maintaining an outright ban on FDI, according to Shanker Singham, President and Chairman of the Competere Foundation for Trade and Competition Policy.
In July 2025, the government relaxed its FDI rules, allowing foreign investment in e-commerce companies that hold their own inventory, provided that it is intended solely for export. Previously, FDI was prohibited in e-commerce companies that maintained their own inventory.
“The concern about the FDI restriction on the type of model you use to invest in India with regard to e-commerce is that you’re determining a particular model and allowing certain firms that don’t have that model not to benefit from the easement to the restriction and other firms that do have that model to benefit from it,” Mr. Singham told The Hindu in an interview.
“I would argue that allowing FDI in the inventory model only for exports is almost worse than having just a blanket investment restriction because you’re selecting models, saying certain models will work, certain other models will not work,” he added.
Cost of restrictions
According to a report by the Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL) at the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade and the Competere Foundation, India still has several policy measures that result in Anti-Competitive Market Distortions (ACMDs).
The report estimates that these ACMDs could result in a combined economic loss of about $173.6 billion for the Indian economy over five years, equivalent to about 4.2% of GDP.
Of this, foreign-investment restrictions are estimated to account for around $127.2 billion. The remaining $46.4 billion is attributed to what the report describes as “competition-policy drift,” under which investors face disproportionately high regulatory requirements.
“These losses fall on India first,” the report said. “They reduce productivity, limit investment, weaken contestability, slow technology diffusion, and reduce the gains available from India’s own domestic reform success.”
Balancing national security
Mr. Singham says that the government’s focus on encouraging manufacturing within India is important, but also says that it should consider whether such measures are worth the cost of the impact they have on competition.
“I understand the government’s focus on encouraging manufacturing for export,” he said. “But, from a pure perspective of the effect on competition, that policy change doesn’t fix the problem. I think what would fix the problem is an elimination of the foreign investment restriction itself.”
He added that the national security reason, as well, must be balanced between its validity and the impact it is having.
Highlighting that national security considerations “are fine up to a point”, Mr. Singham said “national security is like any other regulatory objective.” The key questions are whether it is a legitimate regulatory goal and whether it can be achieved in the least anti-competitive manner possible. according to him.
India, for example, has banned a number of Chinese apps and has imposed restrictions on FDI coming in from countries that share a land border with India, including China.
“If there isn’t a legitimate national security interest, the analysis stops there,” Mr. Singham explained, speaking generally rather than regarding any particular country. “If there is a national security interest, then you’d say, ‘is this the least anti-competitive way of achieving that goal’.”

briefs.headline: Hexaware eyes slice of $900 billion SaaS market with AI-enabled software, even as AI-infused revenue tops 50%
briefs.deck: CEO R. Srikrishna says AI has made custom software fast and economical enough to replace some enterprise SaaS subscriptions
briefs.bodyText:
Hexaware Technologies is going after a slice of the $900 billion global SaaS market, betting that AI has made it cheap and fast enough to build custom software that can replace licensed enterprise applications rather than simply migrate customers from one subscription vendor to another.
“It’s no longer expensive or time consuming to build custom software to replace SaaS. We do it in weeks or months,” CEO R. Srikrishna said during an interaction with reporters.
Mr. Srikrishna said labour is the largest cost in a client’s IT budget, followed by software licensing and cloud, while AI tokens are expected to become the fourth-largest cost by 2027.
To illustrate the economics, Mr. Srikrishna gave a hypothetical example of a customer spending $10 million a year on a large enterprise SaaS platform. Replacing that spend with custom-built software, he said, could cost around $2 million as a one-time investment, though he noted this particular category is not an immediate target area.
However, Hexaware does not expect to displace the entire SaaS market, he said, pointing to regulated industries and compliance-bound clients who will continue relying on licensed software, as well as customers who simply prefer to stay on established platforms.
The clearer opportunity, he said, lies with SaaS products that vendors are sunsetting, and with low-code and no-code use cases where enterprises are more willing to build their own.
Zero License is one of six “zero” pillars, alongside Zero Vulnerability, Zero Tech Debt, Zero Backlog, Zero Defects and Zero Tickets, that Hexaware is packaging under a new AI delivery layer called Zerovity.
The platform is designed to give Hexaware a common context of a client’s business across services that have traditionally been handled in silos.
Mr. Srikrishna likened Zerovity’s deployment model to Tesla, where a customer starts with the core platform and can add individual capabilities as needed.
“You get a car, you turn on features by paying a software fee. That’s the same thought process,” he said. Hexaware would similarly deploy Zerovity as the base platform and allow customers to add or enable individual “zero” capabilities through software.
The CEO said the combined addressable opportunity across the six pillars is roughly $200 billion, while stressing that Hexaware does not view the entire underlying markets as addressable.
More than half of revenue already AI-infused
Mr. Srikrishna disclosed a new figure on how deeply AI has already penetrated Hexaware’s business. “We just put a number for the first time today that greater than 50% of our revenues is already AI-infused,” he said, referring to work in which Hexaware uses AI in delivering services to clients.
Managing token costs
When asked about AI expenditure not appearing as a core part of Hexaware’s overall budget, Mr. Srikrishna said much of the spending is borne by clients because the company often works in clients’ development environments and uses their tokens.
However, he said Hexaware’s Zerovity platform includes a “harness” that selects AI models in real time based on the task. He said model capabilities can differ by about 5%, while costs can differ by as much as 20 times.
He cited one client that had been running out of tokens, forcing developers to return to manually writing code. After Hexaware implemented the harness, he said, the same client had tokens left over at the end of the month.
Revenue deflation
Not all of Hexaware’s six pillars work in the company’s favour financially. Mr. Srikrishna said Zero Tickets and Zero Defects are “deflationary” (reducing revenue from existing services) for its core IT services business, while Zero Backlog is partly deflationary because AI reduces the work required even as it may unlock higher volumes. The remaining pillars, he said, represent new addressable markets.
That erosion is a dynamic Mr. Srikrishna said he is pushing his own sales organisation to get ahead of.
Mr. Srikrishna said the company is asking its sales teams to proactively offer clients lower-cost delivery as AI makes existing IT services more efficient. The logic is that if Hexaware does not reduce the cost of a service itself, a competitor could use AI to do the same work more cheaply and eventually take the business altogether. He said Hexaware intends to offset that pressure by expanding into new lines of work.
“So we are not running away from deflation. But I think we can outrun it by picking new lanes of work,” he said.
Workforce overhaul
The strategy is accompanied by an aggressive internal AI training mandate. Hexaware’s management team must now complete 20 hours of AI learning, up from eight hours previously, while sales employees who fail to complete the training risk losing their bonus, with a second failure resulting in termination, the CEO said.
He said he also expects the industry’s talent profile to shift toward younger, AI-native engineers, even as Hexaware continues to need Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to identify problems that clients need solved, AI architects to design solutions, and engineers to execute them.

briefs.headline: NBFCs stay on growth track as asset quality remains stable: Report
briefs.deck: Non-banking financial companies anticipate steady growth ahead. Credit demand remains robust despite global geopolitical uncertainties. NBFC earnings showed strong growth in the first quarter of FY27. Vehicle financiers experienced accelerated asset under management growth. Gold financiers saw moderated growth and yield pressures.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are likely to maintain steady growth in the near to medium term, with credit demand remaining healthy despite geopolitical uncertainties, according to brokerage firm 360 ONE Capital.
The brokerage said management teams have retained their FY27 and medium-term growth guidance, while asset quality is expected to remain broadly stable.
However, pressure on lending yields and margins, particularly for gold and affordable housing financiers, will remain key monitorables.
NBFC earnings show strong growth in Q1 FY27
NBFCs under 360 ONE Capital’s coverage, excluding power financiers, reported strong earnings in the first quarter of FY27.
Net interest income (NII) grew 23.9 per cent year-on-year, while operating profit increased 24.9 per cent and profit after tax (PAT) rose 36.9 per cent. Aggregate assets under management (AUM) grew around 19 per cent YoY, broadly in line with expectations.
The brokerage said management commentary indicated that credit demand remained resilient, with the West Asia crisis having a limited impact so far.
Early delinquency indicators also showed no discernible asset quality stress from the geopolitical situation or El Nino, while stressed assets remained broadly stable across most lending segments.
Vehicle financiers see stronger AUM growth
Among vehicle financiers, AUM growth accelerated to 16.8 per cent YoY from 16.4 per cent in the previous quarter.
The brokerage attributed the improvement to strong disbursement momentum and said demand remained healthy, with limited impact from monsoons and geopolitical uncertainties.
Housing finance companies (HFCs), however, recorded slower-than-expected AUM growth of 5.6 per cent YoY.
The weaker growth was partly attributed to elevated balance transfers out at LIC Housing Finance. The company subsequently lowered its FY27 loan growth guidance to 8-10 per cent, from 10-12 per cent earlier.
Other prime HFCs maintained their growth outlook, according to 360 ONE Capital.
Gold finance growth moderates, power financiers remain weak
Growth among gold financiers moderated to 47.1 per cent YoY, following stabilisation in gold prices and the implementation of new gold loan guidelines.
The brokerage flagged competitive pressure on yields as a key concern for the segment going forward.
Power financiers remained the weakest segment covered by the brokerage. Their combined loan book grew only 2.3 per cent YoY and declined 0.3 per cent sequentially.
Margins were broadly in line with expectations, although Muthoot Finance recorded a sharper-than-expected compression of around 300 basis points.
Going forward, 360 ONE Capital said the sustainability of net interest margins will remain a key monitorable amid yield pressures, particularly in gold finance and affordable housing finance.

briefs.headline: 29 states vs Meta: How a landmark child safety trial could reshape Facebook, Insta
briefs.deck: Twenty-nine US states are suing Meta, alleging exploitative product design targeting young users. The lawsuit claims Meta concealed internal research about potential harms to teenagers. States seek substantial financial penalties and court-ordered product redesigns for Facebook and Instagram. A former Meta engineer will testify as a key witness in the ongoing trial. This case could significantly…
briefs.bodyText:
Meta is facing a landmark legal challenge in the US that could have far-reaching implications for how Facebook and Instagram are designed and operated, after 29 states accused the company of deliberately creating products that exploit the psychological vulnerabilities of children and teenagers.
The jury trial began this week in federal court in Oakland, California, and is expected to last six to eight weeks. California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey are leading the case on behalf of the 29 states.
The 233-page lawsuit, filed in 2023, alleges that Meta designed and monetised Facebook and Instagram to encourage compulsive use among young people, concealed internal research about potential harms and violated laws protecting children's personal data.
Meta strongly denies the allegations.
What the 29 states are alleging
The states' case centres on four main claims.
The first concerns what they describe as exploitative and addictive product design. The states allege Meta deliberately engineered features to stimulate compulsive engagement and encourage users to spend more time on its platforms.
These features include infinite scrolling, autoplay, persistent push notifications, “likes” and visual filters that the states say can contribute to body image problems.
According to the lawsuit, internal Meta documents show the company studied adolescent brain development, including lower impulse control and greater sensitivity to rewards, and used that knowledge in designing its products.
California deputy attorney general Megan O'Neill described the alleged business model during opening arguments as a process to “hook” users, “hold” them for as long as possible, “harvest” their data and “hide” information about the risks.
The second claim alleges that Meta concealed internal research showing links between Instagram use and depression, anxiety, body image problems and self-harm among teenagers.
Lawyers for the states told jurors that internal documents included statements suggesting the company knew some teenagers were continuing to use Instagram despite negative effects.
The third allegation concerns children's privacy. The states claim Meta collected personal data from children under 13 without obtaining verifiable parental consent, in violation of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act.
The fourth relates to alleged violations of state consumer protection, fair-trading and fraud laws.
Meta rejects allegations
Meta has strongly rejected the claims and argued that the states' case relies on internal documents and emails taken out of context.
During opening arguments, Meta lawyer Paul Schmidt said the company had recognised that some people could struggle with their use of social media and had tried to develop tools to help them.
“There can be no dispute that Meta has both recognised that people can struggle with their use of social media and tried to come up with tools to help them,” Schmidt said.
According to The Guardian, Schmidt also told jurors that Meta had disabled more than 1 million accounts belonging to children under 13 and was “acting in a meaningful way to remove” young users.
A Meta spokesperson said the states were pursuing an “outlandish payout” and argued that their claims were unsubstantiated and that their financial demands were disproportionate.
Damages could run into hundreds of billions
The financial stakes in the case are substantial.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta and lawyers representing the other states told the presiding judge that Meta had warned potential damages could reach $1.4 trillion. However, the states said a more realistic figure would be around $200 billion.
That would be close to the $206 billion settlement reached in 1998 between 52 US state and territory attorneys general and the country's four largest tobacco companies.
The Guardian reported that the states estimate potential damages at up to $200 billion, an amount equivalent to Meta's 2025 annual revenue.
However, the states are seeking more than financial penalties. They also want the court to order changes to how Facebook and Instagram operate.
Could Facebook and Instagram be redesigned?
The states argue that financial penalties alone would not address the alleged harms and are seeking court-ordered changes to Meta's products.
Among the changes they have proposed are removing infinite scrolling for young users and ending what they describe as deceptive representations about platform safety.
A ruling requiring product changes could have implications beyond the US. Maintaining separate, safer versions of Facebook and Instagram exclusively for US users could be technically and economically impractical.
The case could therefore affect how Meta designs its platforms for users in other markets as well, depending on the scope of any eventual court order.
The trial's potential impact extends beyond Meta's financial liability because a court-ordered redesign could affect some of the core features through which users interact with Facebook and Instagram.
Former Meta engineer among key witnesses
One of the states' key witnesses is former Meta safety engineer and whistleblower Arturo Béjar.
Béjar was the first witness called by the government after opening statements. The jury is also expected to hear testimony from Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri and other company executives.
The states' lawyers are expected to rely on internal company documents and witness testimony to support their allegations that Meta knew about potential harms to young users but failed to adequately address them.
Meta, meanwhile, maintains that it has studied the experiences of young users and developed measures intended to support teenagers on its platforms.
Trial comes as countries consider social media safeguards
The case is being closely watched alongside broader efforts to address alleged harms associated with social media.
A report published in The Conversation highlighted a “digital duty of care” as one alternative approach. Under such a system, social media companies would be required to build products with safety standards from the outset rather than governments responding to individual harms through separate laws and regulations.
Australia is among the countries that has already committed to such an approach.
The outcome of the Oakland trial could therefore be significant not only for Meta but also for governments considering how to regulate social media platforms and protect children online.

briefs.headline: Did Press Note 3 relaxations help attract more FDI? | Explained
briefs.deck: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry has said that a total of 29 FDI projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore had been reported to it under its revised framework up to August 10, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
The story so far: The government on Friday (August 21, 2026) said that India had received foreign direct investment (FDI) worth ₹4,895 over just the last few months from companies that have benefitted from recent relaxations made to India’s FDI rules.
The aim of the relaxations was precisely to ease the flow of investments that had earlier been locked out of India.
What was the earlier rule?
The Indian government in April 2020 issued Press Note 3, in which it amended India’s FDI policy. The existing rule at the time said that any entity of Bangladesh and Pakistan could invest in India only after securing Government approval. Press Note 3 widened this stipulation to include any country that shared a land border with India. So, this included Pakistan, China, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Bhutan.
The popular perception is that the government took this decision as a result of border clashes between India and China at Galwan. However, Press Note 3 was issued in April 2020, before those clashes took place in May.
The reason the change was made was to prevent hostile takeovers of companies ailing due to the COVID-19 pandemic. India and a few other countries had noticed that, early on in the pandemic, Chinese companies were buying up majority stakes in companies in these countries whose stock prices had plummeted due to the pandemic. The FDI restriction was aimed at curbing this.
While the origin of the rule was not directly linked to the border clashes, its extension over the years was certainly a result of the frigid relationship between India and China.
What was the relaxation?
In March 2026, the Indian government eased the Press Note 3 restrictions somewhat. It said that FDI from entities would be allowed in India through the automatic route, without needing express government approval, if these entities had less than 10% stake based in countries that share a land border with India.
In other words, companies that had minority and non-controlling stakes held by these land-border countries could invest in India through the easier route.
The government did this because it said that a lot of investment into India had been held up because even companies that had tiny stakes owned by Chinese entities faced stricter restrictions on their investments into India.
“It is expected that the new guidelines will provide clarity and ease of doing business in India, and facilitate investments which can contribute towards greater FDI inflows, access to new technologies, domestic value addition, expansion of domestic firms and integration with global supply chain,” the government had said in March when it eased the rules.
What has been the benefit?
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Friday (August 21, 2026) said that a total of 29 FDI projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore had been reported to it under its revised framework up to August 10, 2026.
It added that these investments span a range of sectors, including information technology, artificial intelligence, information & communication, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, data centres and transport services, among others.
Further, the investments have come from several countries, including Mauritius, the U.S., the Republic of Korea, Japan, Singapore, Luxembourg, and the Cayman Islands.
In relative terms, this investment amount is not all that significant. For instance, it amounts to less than 1% of the total FDI India received in 2025-26. But it is still early days, and for India and FDI, every little bit helps.

briefs.headline: India’s crude import bill surges 41% in July amid West Asia crisis; volumes up 13%
briefs.deck: Episodic events in West Asia had kept prices on benchmark brent crude largely volatile in July this year.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s crude oil import bill surged more than 41% year-on-year to $13.7 billion in July, according to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), as elevated global oil prices amid persistent uncertainty in West Asia pushed up the cost of shipments.
The country’s crude oil imports rose 13.3% in volume terms to 21.4 million metric tonnes (MMT) in July, compared with 18.9 MMT in the same month last year. However, the sharp increase in international crude prices resulted in a significantly higher import outgo.
India’s crude basket averaged $82.04 a barrel in July, up from $70.95 a barrel a year earlier. Benchmark Brent crude prices remained volatile during the month as episodic developments in West Asia continued to influence market sentiment.
Brent crude futures were trading more than 1% higher at around $91.84 a barrel on Tuesday evening following the latest escalation in the region.
LNG imports remain largely stable
India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports increased marginally by 1.5% year-on-year to 2,915 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) in July.
India remains heavily dependent on overseas supplies to meet its energy requirements, with crude oil imports accounting for 88.5% of the country’s total crude oil consumption, according to the provisional PPAC data.
Petroleum product exports rise
Meanwhile, exports of petroleum products by Indian oil-marketing companies increased 10% year-on-year to 5.5 MMT in July.
Revenue from petroleum product exports rose to $5 billion during the month, compared with $3.3 billion a year earlier.
Overall, the country’s net import bill for oil and gas – which is the difference between petroleum products, crude and gas imports; and exports of petroleum products – increased more than 19% on a year-over-year basis to $11.2 billion.

briefs.headline: US-Canada trade standoff: 50% tariff kicks in as Ottawa vows 'dollar-for-dollar' response
briefs.deck: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada fell apart after a three-day face-off. Canada called a halt to discussions, criticizing the US for presenting proposals that were both unfair and detrimental. In a dramatic move, the US introduced hefty tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting Canada to respond with an equal retaliatory measure. This failure to reach an agreement casts…
briefs.bodyText:
The United States called the collapse of three days of intensive trade talks with Canada a “missed opportunity”, as Ottawa suspended negotiations and ordered its team to return, as Washington imposed 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods.
US trade representative Jamieson Greer said Canada had declined to finalize a deal despite what he described as a US offer to give Canada the “best treatment of any major exporter” to the American market. He said new Canadian demands and changes to earlier commitments had disrupted the balance reached during negotiations.
"Tonight, Canada declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week. Despite the US offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days. In addition, Canada is continuing to maintain its prolonged retaliation against the United States, including, among other things, flat-out prohibitions on certain American goods and services," it said
"For decades, Canada has enjoyed the most favorable access to the US market of any country. And from the beginning of President Trump’s trade program, Canada has continued to enjoy the best treatment in the world, even after – like China – retaliating against the United States. This week, the United States agreed to provide even better treatment to Canada, offering significant tariff reductions on steel, aluminum, autos, and lumber," he added.
Also read: 
Canada suspends trade talks with US, PM Carney says will match tariffs 'dollar for dollar'
Further continuing slamming Canada, it said, "The US offer was also forward looking, and included a historic economic and national security partnership to cooperate on export controls, combat transshipment, enhance digital trade, and align certain external tariffs. 
The offer would have led to supply chain coordination on aerospace, complementary actions to address unfair trade practices, critical minerals cooperation, increased enforcement against imports produced with forced labor, and the announcement of formal U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) negotiations."
"This is a missed opportunity for Canada to partner with the United States, which is the fastest growing economy in the G7," Greer claimed.
Meanwhile, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had suspended the talks and directed Canada’s negotiating team to return to Ottawa after last-minute changes to the US proposal were “unfair” and “uneconomic”.
The US imposed 50 per cent tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian products early Saturday. Carney said Canada would match the tariffs “dollar for dollar” to protect Canadian workers and businesses.
The duties cover about 5 per cent of what Canada ships to the US each year and come after Washington and Ottawa failed to resolve differences over tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, automobiles and lumber.
Read more: 
Why Canada suddenly suspended trade talks while Trump said everything was moving smoothly
The breakdown marked a sharp reversal from two days earlier, when officials from both countries appeared close to a compromise. President Donald Trump had extended the tariff deadline by three days to allow negotiations to continue.
No further talks have been scheduled, raising fresh questions over the future of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, which underpins trade across deeply integrated North American supply chains.
The rupture also represents a significant deterioration in relations between two historic allies. The US and Canada traded about $880 billion in goods and services last year, while nearly 72 per cent of Canada’s goods exports went to the US.
Carney said Canada had recognized that “America has changed” and that the two countries would “not return to our old relationship”. He said Ottawa would instead focus on strengthening its domestic economy and diversifying its trade relationships.

stories.headline: AUS vs BAN 2nd Test: Australia lead by 101 runs; Mitchell Starc and Shoriful Islam take 6 wickets each
stories.deck: Mitchell Starc tore through Bangladesh with a six-wicket haul after removing Shadman Islam with the first ball, but Shoriful Islam hit back with six wickets of his own as 18 wickets tumbled on a dramatic first day
stories.bodyText:
Mitchell Starc removed Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam with the first ball of the match and the veteran Australian fast bowler took six wickets in the first innings on a wild first day of the second cricket Test Saturday (August 22, 2026).
Later, Shoriful Islam incredibly matched Starc's total with a six-wicket haul on a day which saw 18 wickets fall.
After Australia won the toss and decided to bowl, with captain Pat Cummins suggesting “the wicket looks pretty good, but if there is any moisture in it, it might be this morning.”
Starc proved Cummins correct and Bangladesh was bowled out for 64 runs shortly after lunch.
The wicket, however, continued to be a challenge for batters well beyond the morning.
In reply, Australia was 165-8 at stumps to lead by 101 runs despite Shoriful Islam's 6-35 total. Cameron Green was one of the not-out batsmen on 51 with Nathan Lyon on 10.
Shadman Islam was caught in the gully off a leading edge to give Starc his record fourth career wicket on the first ball of a match. Starc removed Tanzid Hasan and had captain Najmul Hossain Shanto caught lbw in the third over to leave Bangladesh, which surprisingly won the first test of the two-test series, reeling.
Starc got his fourth wicket when Cameron Green made a grass-top catch to remove Mominul Haque for 9, the only Bangladesh batter to score a run among the first four batters Saturday (August 22). His fifth wicket came when he had Litton Das trapped lbw and his sixth after lunch.
Starc's figures were 6-12 in 10 overs and Cummins finished with three wickets. The Bangladesh total was the lowest while batting first in Australia since 1932 when South Africa was dismissed for 36.
The highest Bangladesh score was by No. 11 batter Shoriful Islam with 14.
“Six (wickets) in the first session, can't beat that,” Starc told his wife, television commentator and former Australia captain Alyssa Healy while walking off the field at lunch. “Obviously a little bit of anger."
Australia announced a 13-man squad earlier this week, with only one change for the second test. It dropped Jake Weatherald and recalled Matt Renshaw, who opened the batting but was out for 8 early in the Australian innings.
The match began under sunny skies at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay, a coastal city in Queensland state about 800 kilometers (500 miles) north of the capital Brisbane.
Bangladesh's first test win in Australia put pressure on national cricket selectors for an overhaul, but the bulk of the aging squad was retained despite being outplayed in Darwin, where the likes of Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Hasan made the most of the tropical conditions.
The two-test “Top End” series starts a heavy 12-month schedule for the Australians that will feature 20 test matches, including tours to South Africa, India and England.

stories.headline: Lando Norris on pole for Dutch Grand Prix as Russell cruises to sprint win
stories.deck: As rain started to fall on the Zandvoort track, McLaren's Norris made the most of his final run to reclaim pole by 0.102 of a second from George Russell, whose Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli — the standings leader — was third
stories.bodyText:
Lando Norris found unexpected pace to beat his rivals and the weather to take pole position for the Dutch Grand Prix on Saturday (August 22, 2026) after George Russell took a sprint race win on Formula 1's return from its mid-season break.
As rain started to fall on the Zandvoort track, McLaren's Norris made the most of his final run to reclaim pole by 0.102 of a second from Russell, whose Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli — the standings leader — was third.
“A little surprised, honestly, but a decent lap," said Norris, who'd been critical of his car in the earlier sprint race and credited McLaren with making the right changes.
“We had to try something because what we had before wasn't going to be enough," he said, adding the changes were small but "enough to give me some confidence.” Norris won the last race in Hungary on July 26 but was deflated after the sprint, saying McLaren wasn't competitive at all in slower corners.
Russell is rebuilding his title challenge after losing ground to Antonelli last month and said it was “a real joy” to drive in qualifying. The plan now is to “get in my groove again and try to fight with them tomorrow," he added.
Lewis Hamilton lost ground to Antonelli in the standings in the sprint race. His difficult day continued with fifth in qualifying.
Russell takes sprint victoryThe sprint race was a display of domination from Russell, who started from pole position, quickly built a gap to Norris in second and managed the pace from there, taking his first win since the Austrian Grand Prix in June.
“Obviously a great start to the weekend,” he said.
Charles Leclerc snatched second off Norris with a daring pass into the inside of the first corner with six laps to go, but couldn't get close enough to try passing Russell.
Norris held off a late charge from Antonelli to stay third as the Italian pulled out of a potential overtaking move on the final lap.
“We just don't have the pace in general, especially in the slow-speed corners,” Norris said.
Fourth-place Antonelli, starting fifth after car damage in qualifying, still managed to extend his standings lead by three more points to 53 because Hamilton could only manage seventh for Ferrari.
Long-awaited rain arrives seconds too late to shake up sprintF1 still hasn't had a wet race this year but came tantalizingly close as rain fell as the drivers were heading back to the pits, seconds after the sprint finished.
“If there was one more lap it would have been a very, potentially, different end to the race so I'm glad the rain came when it did,” Russell said.
While it stayed dry, overtaking was difficult, even in a year where the cars' electrical power has made back-and-forth passes common. The overtakes by Leclerc and Antonelli were the only changes of position anywhere in the top 11 finishers. (AP) PDS

stories.headline: Serena Williams teams up with Carlos Alcaraz for US Open mixed doubles comeback
stories.deck: In an electrifying pairing, tennis legends Serena Williams and rising star Carlos Alcaraz will join forces for the mixed doubles at the US Open. This unique collaboration between champions from different eras promises to captivate fans, especially as Alcaraz aims to reclaim his singles title after injury recovery. With a lineup of elite competitors, this mixed doubles event is poised to be a…
stories.bodyText:
Serena Williams is set to make her return to the US Open in a blockbuster mixed doubles partnership with Carlos Alcaraz. The United States Tennis Association (USTA) announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz have received a wild card into the US Open mixed doubles main draw, with the event set to begin on Tuesday.
The partnership brings together two generations of Grand Slam champions and is expected to be one of the biggest attractions of this year's tournament.
Serena returns to Flushing Meadows
The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion will be back at the US Open for the first time since 2022. Williams returned to competitive tennis this summer after a break from the sport. She played singles at Wimbledon and later teamed up with her older sister Venus Williams in doubles at the Cincinnati Open.
It remains unclear whether Serena will also compete in the women's singles draw. The USTA still has one women's singles wild card available, although Williams has not confirmed whether she intends to use it.
Alcaraz returns after injury
Alcaraz, meanwhile, is set to return to action after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury. The Spaniard recently confirmed that he will defend his US Open singles title, making his mixed doubles partnership with Williams an additional attraction at Flushing Meadows.
The 2026 mixed doubles event will feature a revamped format designed to bring some of tennis' biggest stars into the competition. Matches will be played in a best-of-three format with sets decided at four games, no-ad scoring and a 10-point match tiebreak if required.
The winning team will also share a $1 million prize.
Star-studded mixed doubles field
Williams and Alcaraz are part of an impressive field featuring several high-profile combinations. Former world No. 1s Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic will form another headline pairing, while Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud are also set to compete.
American stars Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz will team up, while reigning champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori will return to defend their title.
For Williams, the US Open holds a special place in her career. She has won the tournament multiple times and previously captured the US Open mixed doubles title in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi.

stories.headline: Dhols, chants and belief: How Delhi turned a World Championships semi-final into a homecoming
stories.deck: A packed Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium created an unforgettable atmosphere as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand battled China's top seeds in the BWF World Championships semi-finals. Chants, dhols and unwavering support drove the Indian pair throughout their 64-minute contest. Though the eventual bronze medallists fell short, Delhi's passionate crowd emerged as one of the tournament's defining…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Outside the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium on Saturday, the thermometer read 33 degrees Celsius. It wasn't difficult to break into a sweat. The road that had been largely empty throughout the week was bustling, and the question on most lips was, 'Where is Gate 7?', 'Bhaiya World Championships ke liye kaunsa gate hai?' [Which gate for the 
BWF World Championships
?]
Inside the 15,000-seater facility, half of which was in use for the tournament, the AC had been cranked up. Coincidentally, it matched the intensity and atmosphere of the crowd that had filled the stadium to the brim.
The occasion was the women's doubles semi-final featuring Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Pullela Gopichand. For the 64 minutes that the Indians battled in a three-game contest, winning the first game, the crowd stayed behind them every step of the way.
"Together we rise higher," read a poster from a young fan that was later presented to Jolly. The poster, featuring both players, said, "Two rackets. One Dream. One Nation," and that was the feeling inside the venue.
Treesa Jolly with a poster gifted by a young fan. (Photo Courtesy: Tanuj Lakhina)
"C'mon Pullela!" and "Jolly Jolly" rang out in sections whenever the Indian team earned a point. "Maar! Maar na!" echoed, without rehearsal, whenever the point was there for the taking and a smash looked inevitable. Equally loud were collective moans and "Noooos!" whenever the point went the way of the World No. 
1 and top seeds Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China.
Vadodara native Dr. Harshil was living every moment of it. After buying tickets weeks in advance, he took an overnight train from Gujarat and arrived earlier in the day for the World Championships. The fact that it was for a monumental occasion, India winning a medal for the 12th edition running, was a happy coincidence.
A packed Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium created an unforgettable atmosphere as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand battled China's top seeds in the BWF World Championships semi-finals. (Photo Courtesy:  BAI)
Dr. Harshil doesn't play badminton but stays abreast of the sport and watches every tournament on TV. Also a keen watcher of athletics, he was most enthused about the match featuring Chou Tien Chen and was inspired by the Taiwanese shuttler's battle and recovery from colorectal cancer.
But in that moment, as the vociferous crowd erupted and sat down near simultaneously, he couldn't keep his eyes away from Court 1.
The DJ would ring out at the breaks, celebrating every smash, every drop and every shot landing wide. As far as partisan crowds go, this was a living example. A set of dhols, placed in the second tier of the stadium, would make their presence felt every now and then.
India's Gayatri Gopichand Pullela clicks a selfie with spectators during the match between India and China in the women's doubles semifinal at the BWF Badminton World Championships at Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)
In the second set, as the Chinese pairing started to pick up the lead and took advantage of rising errors from the Indians, the crowd intensity, somehow, only got louder. The defiance of the Indians on the court was being matched by the decibel level of the crowd.
And by the third set, as the Chinese piled on the pressure, with the Indians losing their intensity and coherence, the crowd saw the effort wane. The fans had their voice at the start, but with the World No. 1s plucking points in a row, the spectators started to walk towards the exit doors.
'Focus. Believe. Together. Victory' also read the poster that Treesa carried with her. On the day, the crowd believed in the 23-year-old Indians. It came together, and in massive numbers. The victory, however, eluded them and the fans. But the venue, which had been the butt of jokes during the India Open in January, had just made itself count.

briefs.headline: Men’s hockey World Cup: Dutch enter semis; India on the brink of elimination
briefs.deck: The home side punishes Harmanpreet & Co. on the counter; the former champion is languishing at the bottom of Pool E but has a slim hope, thanks to Argentina’s 3-1 victory over England
briefs.bodyText:
India got a close up display on how to come up with a clinical performance at the hands of the Netherlands.
With six minutes to go, Manpreet Singh dawdled on the ball allowing Jorrit Croon to rob the ball and slip in Thijs van Dam. The forward flicked it over Mohith H.S., controlled it on the run, before slapping the ball into the net to finish off India in style..
In front of a packed Wagener Stadion, Netherlands sealed its place in the semifinal of the World Cup with a 3-1 win, pushing India to the brink of elimination here on Saturday. Argentina got the better of England 3-1 later in the day to boost its qualification chances.
Placed last, India needs to beat Argentina by a margin of four goals or more in its final Pool E match on Monday and hope that the Dutch defeat England on the same day.
Requiring a win, India put up a spirited fight, getting its tactics spot on to make the home side work hard, but familiar troubles in field play plagued Craig Fulton’s men. But the Dutch, picked apart India with three field goals, two of them coming from devastating counter-attacks.
Of the four matches in the tournament, this was India’s best start. Fulton’s side was sharper on the ball, controlling possession, not allowing the Dutch to play their flick passing game.
However, India, too, didn’t find space in the circle, struggling to find the right connections in field play. Dilpreet Singh came close but his deflected effort was booted away by Derk Meijer.
After trading blows again in the third quarter, the Dutch found momentum, before taking the lead. From a loose ball in the circle, Tijmen Rayenga’s shot-cum-pass was flicked in past Suraj Karkera by Duco Telgenkamp.
Chasing the equaliser, Harmanpreet Singh and Sanjay, unable to bypass the Netherlands press, were exchanging passes at the halfway line before the latter tried to force the initiative with a fizzed-in pass but went out of bounds.
Seconds later, the Netherlands turned defence into attack with three passes. Tjep Hoedemakers deflected the ball into the goal from a fierce Koen Bijen slapshot into the circle.
India responded immediately through Harmanpreet, finding the left bottom corner with his side’s sixth and final PC to halve the deficit.
But India’s hopes of a comeback were extinguished when Manpreet’s error was punished by van Dam.
The result: Netherlands 3 (Telgenkamp 40, Hoedemakers 50, van Dam 54) bt India 1 (Harmanpreet 51-pc).

The statisticians were made to work overtime on Saturday as the Tamil Nadu Premier League Season 10 playoff race delivered a close finish.

Two spots were up for grabs when the final first-round match between playoff aspirants Nellai Royal Kings and Panthers got underway at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium here. At the end of it, the Madurai side not only sealed a Qualifier 1 berth with a comprehensive 72-run victory but also lent a helping hand to the Tiruppur outfit.
While the Royal Kings’ target for a top-two seat was 199, the magic number they chased was 144, a score which would have guaranteed them a path to the next stage. But a collapse of epic proportions – from 92 for three to 126 all-out – led to its elimination.
Shoaib Mohammed Khan (65, 43b, 6x4, 3x6 and two for 20) came up with a Player-of-the-Match show while a number of other players also contributed to the big win.
The Tiruppur team’s fate was no longer in its hands after it suffered a 45-run defeat to SKM Salem Spartans earlier in the day. With the result, Spartans avoided the ignominy of going winless in this campaign and Kovai Kings confirmed a final-four spot.

briefs.headline: Badminton World championships | Battle lines drawn for singles crown
briefs.deck: While Naraoka faces Lanier for the men’s title, the women’s final brings together Se-young and Yamaguchi
briefs.bodyText:
The men’s singles final will crown a new badminton World champion. The women’s title clash will pit the defending champion against a three-time victor.
In men’s singles, 21-year-old Alex Lanier will face Japan’s Kodai Naraoka for a world title neither has won before, with both guaranteed their first World championships medal. Lanier beat Canada’s Victor Lai 16-21, 21-13, 21-14.
The Frenchman has repeatedly had to recover from difficult positions during his run. Against Victor, as in his quarterfinal against Kunlavut Vitidsarn, he found a way to steady himself and change the momentum.“
At some point you need to trust how good you are,” Lanier said after the semifinal. Naraoka took a different route. The Japanese lost the opening game 17-21 to veteran Chou Tien Chen before taking control, winning the next two 21-11, 21-10. Chou, 36, had been chasing a second record after becoming the oldest men’s singles medallist in World championships history, but Naraoka’s patience and rallying eventually ended that bid.
The women’s final brings together An Se-young and Akane Yamaguchi, with Se-young holding a 19-15 advantage. Yamaguchi moved through with a composed 21-12, 21-17 victory over Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong, becoming the only women’s singles player to win six World championships medals.
Se-young survived a gruelling opening game against Wang Zhi Yi, edging it 24-22 before closing out the second 21-16. She appeared to struggle with her left leg late in the second set, but stayed in the contest and sealed victory with a net dribble at 20-16.
The Japanese star now stands between Se-young and a second straight title. “I’m looking forward to how I perform,” said Se-young.

briefs.bodyText:
Rohit Yadav spectacularly pushed his personal best to 87.68m to take the men’s javelin gold while 19-year-old sprinter Abinaya Rajarajan gave a dazzling performance to clock 11.34s and win the women’s 100m with a National under-20 record in the $75,000 World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meet at the Kalinga Stadium on Saturday.
Vithya Ramraj sparkled to record her season’s best 51.96 to clinch the women’s 400m gold.
In the preparatory phase for next month’s Asian Games, long jumpers M. Sreeshankar (8.07m) and Ancy Sojan (6.71m) were among the nine Indians who won gold.
Rohit, who managed 81.56m to finish seventh in the Commonwealth Games, overcame a slip in the second throw to register 81.82m in his penultimate attempt. A more consistent Yashvir logged 82.94m to regain the lead. But, Rohit improved upon his previous best 87.05m, achieved at the inter-State meet here in June, in his final effort. His new mark is the fourth-best in the World this season, just behind Neeraj Chopra (88.05m).
“I gave it my all in the end. I hope to replicate it in the Asiad,” said Rohit.
Abinaya , who recovered from injuries she received at the Asian Indoor meet in February, ran in good rhythm to regain the National under-20 record, which she had held earlier with 11.54, from Nipam (11.53). “I was about to cry towards the end as I knew I was going to break the record,” said Abinaya, thanking her father Rajarajan and coach Sreenivasan Ramaiah.
